TEST-M1-STORY-174

Design decisions to confirm before build

Two product decisions are still open. The screens that follow pick one reasonable default for each so the rest of the flow can be reviewed — swap them once the product owner decides.

For reviewers only — not shown in the product

1. Who submits the request?

This design assumes employee self-service: the signed-in employee submits and cancels their own requests, and that's the flow on the "My time off" screen. If HR/Managers log requests on an employee's behalf instead, the "Request time off" form needs an employee picker and the actor changes. Either way, the "Team time off requests" screen stays HR/Manager-facing and read-only, since that part of the flow doesn't depend on the answer.

2. What happens when a request exceeds the balance?

This design assumes an over-balance request is allowed through with a warning, landing as pending for review, rather than being blocked outright. Try choosing "Personal" (2 days available) with a longer date range in the request form a few screens ahead to see the warning.
